hook_text: Why is there snow on a mountain almost on the equator?
clip_script: Kilimanjaro, three degrees from the equator, nearly six thousand metres high, with ice on top. Why? Because every thousand metres up is about six and a half degrees colder. That is one tool. Here are the others. Latitude: high sun, hot; low sun, cold. Pressure belts: rising air makes rain, sinking air makes deserts. The sea: coasts stay mild, interiors swing hot and cold. Currents: the warm Agulhas makes Durban steamy, the cold Benguela keeps Port Nolloth dry. Mountains: rain on one side, a rain shadow on the other. Six tools. Every climate on Earth can be explained with them, from the Namib to Cape Town's winter rain.
visual_style: A whiteboard toolbox opening, with each tool drawn as a labelled icon: a sun at different angles, rising and sinking arrows, a wave, a thermometer on a mountain, red and blue current arrows, and a cloud over a ridge.
mood: Curious and confident, like a detective solving a case.
pacing: One tool every few seconds, then a quick montage of places being explained.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain any climate with six tools.
